title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 150
paragraphs: After a naval force had thus gone against Samos, the Babylonians revolted, being exceedingly well prepared for it. For during the whole reign of the Magian and the rising of the seven—and throughout the attendant confusion—they had been preparing themselves for the siege of their city; and somehow it happened that they were not observed while doing so. When they at last openly revolted, they did as follows. After setting apart their mothers first, each man also set apart one woman for himself—whomever he chose of his own household—and they gathered all the rest together and killed them by suffocation. Each man set apart the one already mentioned to serve as bread-maker, and they suffocated the rest so that these might not consume their provisions.
